items.followUp: Define a polymer and give two examples.

rubric.why: Identifies macromolecules as large molecules made from smaller units.
rubric.description: Defines a macromolecule by its size and its smaller constituent units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Names two valid examples of macromolecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

modelAnswer: Macromolecules are large molecules formed by the joining of many smaller units.

items.followUp: Name the vegetative and reproductive organs of a rose plant.

rubric.why: Identifies the vegetative organs of the plant.
rubric.description: Names the vegetative organs of mustard.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for roots, stem and leaves.

rubric.why: Identifies the reproductive organ of mustard.
rubric.description: Names the reproductive organ of mustard.

modelAnswer: The vegetative organs of mustard are roots, stem and leaves.
The reproductive organ is the flower.

items.followUp: Differentiate between simple diffusion and osmosis.

rubric.why: States the direction of diffusion and distinguishes its route from facilitated diffusion.
rubric.description: Describes diffusion as movement from higher to lower concentration without transport proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction and route.

rubric.why: States the direction of facilitated diffusion and identifies its protein-assisted route.
rubric.description: Describes facilitated diffusion as movement from higher to lower concentration through membrane proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction and protein-assisted route.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the movement of substances from higher to lower concentration directly through the membrane, without transport proteins.
Facilitated diffusion is movement from higher to lower concentration through specific membrane proteins; neither process requires energy.
